title: Phase 2: request history, reset, and verification
objective: Implement request history read/clear, the atomic full reset, and the verify endpoint with its fixed failure shape, codes, and ordering.
nonGoals: no interaction-derived failure not covered by §41.9

blockers.summary: §41.9 does not define where a null-requestSequence interaction-derived failure (e.g. journal_full) sorts.
blockers.detail: §41.9 fixes group ordering: interaction-derived failures by request sequence ascending, then expectation failures by registration index ascending; it separately allows sticky failures with requestSequence: null. It does not say where those null-sequence interaction-derived failures belong within group 1. Implementation and its doc comment place them after all sequenced interaction-derived failures and before expectation failures; no vector discriminates.
blockers.recommendation: Resolved by owner ruling + system_one second opinion (0.95): null-sequence interaction-derived failures sort after sequenced ones and before expectation failures. Recommend writing this sentence into §41.9.

nextAction: refresh the five stage artifacts onto the new task fingerprint, then verify and close
notes: scope amendment 2026-09-29 (PM): §41.7 requires method/path on every request-history record; the engine journal has no source. Approved host-populated exchange.Metadata keys "method" and "target" (precedent: host already writes Metadata["error"]), adding internal/host/http/server.go to allowedFiles. Engine core and its journal type stay untouched. Host control-plane routing (/__fake/ delegation) remains a separate recorded gap, out of scope for FJ-021.

scope amendment 2, 2026-09-29 (PM): Option B is unworkable as written because internal/engine/journal.go cloneExchange reassigns exchange.Metadata to a fresh map before ranging over it, so every recorded exchange loses Metadata (the host's Metadata["error"] is already silently dropped). Approved a minimal correctness fix inside cloneExchange (copy into a local map, then assign) plus a regression test, and added internal/engine/journal.go to allowedFiles. No new engine fields; journal record type unchanged; defensive-copy semantics must be preserved.
